finalText:
This is a small Node service — five files, no framework, no database. Here's how a request flows.

```mermaid
graph LR
  A[server.js] -->|verifies Bearer token| B[auth.js]
  A --> C[routes.js]
  C -->|reads| D[cache.js]
  C -->|writes| E[store.js]
  D --> E
```

`server.js` is the raw `http` entry point: it checks the `Authorization` header via `auth.js` (HMAC-signed `userId.signature` tokens) and 401s anyone who fails. Everything past that goes to `routes.js`, a plain lookup table of `"METHOD /path"` to handler functions. Reads (`GET /users`, `GET /orders`) go through `cache.js`, a 256-entry LRU with no expiry of its own. Writes (`POST /orders`) go straight to `store.js`, an in-memory map where every record just expires 15 minutes after it's written.

One thing worth knowing before you touch this: the comment in `routes.js` says writes "invalidate the affected keys," but `putOrder` never actually clears the matching cache entry. So a cached `orders:<userId>` list can go stale for up to 15 minutes after a new order is placed — worth checking if anyone's hit that.

Open `src/routes.js` if you want to start there.
